Use case: scientific-educational. Asset type: photographic scene contact sheet for an Arabic/English child science app. EXACT FOUR ROWS and FOUR COLUMNS, sixteen equally sized SQUARE photos in a regular 4x4 grid. Thin white gutters only, no border outside. Request high-resolution square contact sheet 2048 by 2048. Warm light wooden tabletop, soft natural indoor light, neutral pale wall. Adult hands with blue sleeves only when relevant, no faces. Safe large toys, acrylic instead of glass, sealed magnet, shallow little water. Every row tells ONE activity: columns 1 and 2 are condition A action then visible result; columns 3 and 4 condition B action then result. Same camera angle, same apparatus proportions and same objects across all four panels in each row. Preserve unchanged variables strictly. Each result panel must retain the apparatus of the preceding action panel. Show physical differences clearly, no arrows, text, labels, numerals, symbols or decorative graphics. Photorealistic, not illustration. Show the entire relevant setup in every panel; avoid cropped apparatus.  Critical scene constraints: Row1 same sealed magnet attracts steel spoon with and without a THIN vertical paper sheet; keep distance same. Row2 same dense modelling clay amount: BALL SINKS to clear tray bottom; reshaped wide hollow boat floats at water surface with dry interior. Row3 same large plastic boat: light large dough load floats high, increased load lowers boat and water enters. Row4 single large block on flat board balanced on central broad foam fulcrum: centered block board level, moved to edge board tips downward at that edge.
ROW 1 Does paper block a magnet?: COLUMN 1: The adult brings the magnet close to the spoon.; COLUMN 2: The spoon moved in this scene.; COLUMN 3: We place thin paper between the magnet and spoon.; COLUMN 4: The spoon also moved through the paper.. Hold constant: The magnet, spoon and approach distance.
ROW 2 Dough shaped as a ball and boat: COLUMN 1: The adult places a dense dough ball in water.; COLUMN 2: The ball reached the bottom in the scene.; COLUMN 3: We shape the same piece into a wide boat and place it gently.; COLUMN 4: The boat stayed at the surface in the scene.. Hold constant: Amount of dough, water and room temperature.
ROW 3 I add a boat load: COLUMN 1: We put a light load in a large plastic boat.; COLUMN 2: The boat stayed afloat in the scene.; COLUMN 3: The adult adds a large piece of dough to the same boat.; COLUMN 4: The boat sank lower and water entered in the scene.. Hold constant: The boat, load position and water.
ROW 4 A load at the centre and edge: COLUMN 1: We put a large block at the centre of a supported board.; COLUMN 2: The board stayed balanced in the scene.; COLUMN 3: We move the same block toward an edge.; COLUMN 4: The board tilted toward the load.. Hold constant: The board, support and load.

ROW 1 A narrow and a wide base: COLUMN 1: We build a low tower with a narrow base.; COLUMN 2: The tower tilted after a gentle touch in the scene.; COLUMN 3: We widen the base and keep the same height.; COLUMN 4: The tower stayed upright after the touch in the scene.. Hold constant: Tower height, blocks and touch position.
ROW 2 I move bridge supports closer: COLUMN 1: We span a card sheet across supports far apart.; COLUMN 2: The sheet bent under the block in the scene.; COLUMN 3: We move the supports closer and use the same block.; COLUMN 4: The sheet bent less in the scene.. Hold constant: The sheet, load and its position.
ROW 3 One paper layer and more layers: COLUMN 1: We place one paper layer over low supports.; COLUMN 2: The paper sagged under the block in the scene.; COLUMN 3: We add layers of the same paper.; COLUMN 4: The paper stayed higher under the same load in the scene.. Hold constant: Paper type, gap and load.
ROW 4 I mix two water colours: COLUMN 1: We place yellow and blue water in separate cups.; COLUMN 2: We see the colours separately.; COLUMN 3: The adult mixes both waters in one container.; COLUMN 4: Green appeared in the scene.. Hold constant: The two colour types and amounts.

Row3 large white paper towel end above blue water stays dry, then end dipped in blue water with visible wet blue rise up the strip after waiting. Row4 same large floating foam block in same clear plastic tray: low water block low, higher water raises floating block, water level actually rises, block remains floating.
ROW 1 I mix oil and water, then wait: COLUMN 1: The adult turns a sealed bottle containing a little oil and water.; COLUMN 2: We see scattered droplets after mixing.; COLUMN 3: We stand the bottle upright and wait with the adult.; COLUMN 4: An oil layer appeared above the water in the scene.. Hold constant: The bottle and amounts of oil and water.
ROW 2 I tilt a water channel: COLUMN 1: The adult puts a little water in a level channel.; COLUMN 2: Water stayed near the pouring point in the scene.; COLUMN 3: We tilt the channel gently toward a container.; COLUMN 4: Water reached the lower container.. Hold constant: The channel, water and pouring point.
ROW 3 Does paper touch the water?: COLUMN 1: We hold a paper towel strip above water without touching it.; COLUMN 2: The strip stayed dry.; COLUMN 3: We lower the strip tip into coloured water.; COLUMN 4: Wetness climbed the paper after waiting in the scene.. Hold constant: The paper, cup, water amount and observation time.
ROW 4 I put an object in water: COLUMN 1: We observe water in a stable clear container.; COLUMN 2: This is the water level before adding the object.; COLUMN 3: The adult lowers a large clean object into the water.; COLUMN 4: The level rose without adding water.. Hold constant: The container and water amount.

Critical scene constraints: Row1 same upright large opaque square, white screen and flashlight: flashlight far creates smaller shadow, close creates larger shadow. Row2 flashlight and acrylic mirror direct spot on wall then mirror turned spot shifts. Row3 same flashlight aimed white paper: near produces smaller bright patch, farther produces larger softer patch. Row4 same large sponge held above shallow bowl: dry barely wet no water drip, saturated sponge being gently squeezed produces water drips into bowl.
ROW 1 I change shadow size: COLUMN 1: We move the toy close to the fixed flashlight.; COLUMN 2: A larger shadow appeared on the wall.; COLUMN 3: We move the same toy close to the wall.; COLUMN 4: A smaller shadow appeared on the wall.. Hold constant: The toy, flashlight and wall.
ROW 2 I face a mirror toward a toy: COLUMN 1: We turn the safe mirror away from the toy.; COLUMN 2: The toy reflection did not appear from our position.; COLUMN 3: We face the mirror toward the toy without moving the toy.; COLUMN 4: The toy reflection appeared from our position.. Hold constant: The toy, mirror and viewing position.
ROW 3 I move a flashlight closer: COLUMN 1: The adult holds a flashlight near white paper.; COLUMN 2: A small light spot appeared.; COLUMN 3: The adult moves the flashlight farther away without changing its direction.; COLUMN 4: A wider spot appeared in this scene.. Hold constant: The flashlight, its direction and paper.
ROW 4 A damp and a wetter sponge: COLUMN 1: We wet the sponge with a little water and squeeze gently.; COLUMN 2: A few drops fell in the scene.; COLUMN 3: We add more water to the same sponge.; COLUMN 4: More drops fell when squeezed in the scene.. Hold constant: The sponge, squeezing action and tray.

ROW 1 I build a folded bridge: COLUMN 1: We span a flat sheet across supports.; COLUMN 2: The sheet sagged under the block in the scene.; COLUMN 3: We fold the paper like a fan and repeat the test.; COLUMN 4: The folds supported the block in the scene.. Hold constant: The sheet, gap and load.
ROW 2 I build an arch bridge: COLUMN 1: We place flat card between supports.; COLUMN 2: The centre bent under the block in the scene.; COLUMN 3: The adult arches the card and secures both ends.; COLUMN 4: The arch kept supporting the block in the scene.. Hold constant: The card, load and gap.
ROW 3 I add a middle support: COLUMN 1: We place a paper bridge over end supports.; COLUMN 2: The bridge centre sagged under the load.; COLUMN 3: We add a low support under the centre.; COLUMN 4: The centre stayed higher with the support.. Hold constant: The bridge, load and end supports.
ROW 4 I test a board overhang: COLUMN 1: We leave a short board end beyond its support.; COLUMN 2: The board stayed stable with the load in the scene.; COLUMN 3: We lengthen the overhang and repeat with the same load.; COLUMN 4: The board tilted in the scene.. Hold constant: The board, support and load at the end.

Row3 square cardboard frame without diagonal brace becomes parallelogram when gently pushed, adding diagonal cardboard brace leaves square stable. ROW 2 I build a balance and change distance: COLUMN 1: We place matching loads at equal distances from the centre.; COLUMN 2: The balance board stayed level in the scene.; COLUMN 3: We move one load farther from the centre.; COLUMN 4: The board tilted toward the farther load.. Hold constant: The board, support and both loads.

Hold constant: The frame, joints and push position.

Hold constant: The sheet, column height and load.

Hold constant: The cart, track start and fan action.

Hold constant: The track, ball and release point.

Hold constant: The water, pieces and pouring position.

Hold constant: The cups, paper, water and waiting time.

Hold constant: The container, stick and viewing position.
